subtopicTitle: Thin film interference — reflected and transmitted

cards.front: State the rule for phase shift of π upon reflection from an interface.
cards.back: A phase shift of π occurs when light reflects off an interface from lower to higher refractive index; no shift occurs from higher to lower index.

cards.front: What is the optical path difference for a ray traversing a thin film of thickness t and index n at normal incidence?
cards.back: The optical path difference is 2nt (round trip).

cards.front: For an air-film-air soap film (n_film > 1), give the condition for destructive interference in reflected light at normal incidence.
cards.back: 2nt = mλ (m = 0,1,2,...) because net π phase difference from reflections reverses the usual condition.

cards.front: For the same soap film, give the condition for constructive interference in reflected light.
State the interference condition for transmitted light through a thin film (normal incidence) and explain its relation to reflection.
cards.back: Transmitted: constructive when 2nt = mλ. Conditions are complementary to reflection due to energy conservation (no absorption).

cards.front: Derive the minimum thickness t for an antireflection coating (air-glass, MgF₂ film n=1.38) at λ=550 nm.
cards.back: Require destructive reflection: t = λ/(4n) = 550/(4×1.38) ≈ 100 nm. Phase shift occurs at both interfaces so quarter-wave gives net destructive interference.

cards.front: Write the general condition for constructive reflection from a thin film at angle θ (inside film).
cards.back: 2 n t cos θ = (m + 1/2) λ (adjusted for net phase shift of π) or 2 n t cos θ = m λ (no net phase shift).

cards.front: Why does interference vanish for films much thicker than λ?
cards.back: Source coherence length is finite; path difference exceeds coherence length so phase relation is lost and intensities add incoherently.
